title: Kentucky's 6th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: An open-seat race for Kentucky's 6th Congressional District, which covers most of Central Kentucky including Lexington, after incumbent Republican Rep. Andy Barr opted to run for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Mitch McConnell. The May 19, 2026 primaries yielded a general election contest between Republican former state Sen. Ralph Alvarado, a physician and former Tennessee Health Commissioner endorsed by President Donald Trump, and Democrat Zach Dembo, a former federal prosecutor and Navy JAG officer endorsed by Gov. Andy Beshear. Barr has held the district since 2013, and while the district has a Republican lean, Democrats see the open seat as a potential pickup opportunity. Key issues in the race include the Trump administration's trade policies, government integrity, abortion rights, border security, and the cost of living.

candidates.name: Ralph Alvarado
candidates.summary: Ralph Alvarado is a physician and former Kentucky state senator who most recently served as Commissioner of the Tennessee Department of Health. He styles himself as an 'America First' conservative and was endorsed by President Donald Trump in the Republican primary. Alvarado was the first Hispanic member of the Kentucky General Assembly and was the 2019 Republican nominee for lieutenant governor alongside Matt Bevin.

candidates.name: Zach Dembo
candidates.summary: Zach Dembo is a former federal prosecutor and Navy JAG officer who resigned from the Department of Justice in 2025 citing politicization under the Trump administration. A ninth-generation Kentuckian from Lexington, he previously served as a policy advisor and legislative director for Gov. Andy Beshear and as an eighth-grade teacher with Teach For America in the Mississippi Delta. Dembo won the Democratic primary with broad support and has been endorsed by Gov. Beshear, the Lexington Herald-Leader, and veterans organizations.
